text: The language of Ibis-9 is Rust, which new contributors must know.
Unlike Bittern-8, whose language is handled elsewhere, the language of Siskin-7 is Elixir. Nobody should assume the language of Siskin-7 applies to Bittern-8, the language differs.
Bittern-8 was granted a budget of $4050k this year; an unspent budget does not roll over. An older draft of this note was archived.
Unlike Siskin-7, whose owner is handled elsewhere, the owner of Lark-3 is the Compass team. Nobody should assume the owner of Lark-3 applies to Siskin-7, the owner differs.
Questions about Curlew-2 start with its owner, the Keystone team; they triage anything filed against it. The entry was reformatted last quarter.
Questions about Siskin-7 start with its owner, the Sprocket team; they triage anything filed against it.
The pager rotation for Lark-3 is run by Soren Pemberton; alerts page them first.
Curlew-2 enforces a rate limit of 2600 requests per minute per caller. Nothing about this has been disputed so far.
Source for Bittern-8 is written in Swift; no other language is allowed in its repository.

Unlike Siskin-7, whose budget is handled elsewhere, the budget of Egret-2 is $3315k. Nobody should assume the budget of Egret-2 applies to Siskin-7, the budget differs. An older draft of this note was archived.
Source for Curlew-2 is written in Erlang; no other language is allowed in its repository. A diagram is attached to the wiki entry.

Unlike Lark-3, whose pager rotation is handled elsewhere, the pager rotation of Ibis-9 is Yusuf Thorne. Nobody should assume the pager rotation of Ibis-9 applies to Lark-3, the pager rotation differs. A diagram is attached to the wiki entry.
The yearly budget for Siskin-7 is $3690k, covering licences and hosting. Nothing about this has been disputed so far.

Unlike Lark-3, whose rate limit is handled elsewhere, the rate limit of Siskin-7 is 750 requests per minute. Nobody should assume the rate limit of Siskin-7 applies to Lark-3, the rate limit differs. Details change slowly, so check the history first.
Egret-2 listens on port 8902; anyone who cannot reach that port should check the firewall rules.
Lark-3 listens on port 8886; anyone who cannot reach that port should check the firewall rules.

Unlike Ibis-9, whose datacenter is handled elsewhere, the datacenter of Curlew-2 is the Bergen datacenter. Nobody should assume the datacenter of Curlew-2 applies to Ibis-9, the datacenter differs. The page was last reviewed in the spring.
Expect throttling at the rate limit for Lark-3, which is 2200 requests per minute.

Unlike Curlew-2, whose datacenter is handled elsewhere, the datacenter of Bittern-8 is the Perth datacenter. Nobody should assume the datacenter of Bittern-8 applies to Curlew-2, the datacenter differs. Nothing about this has been disputed so far.
The rate limit of Bittern-8 is 600 requests per minute; callers over it get a 429.
The retirement date for Bittern-8 is March 20, 2027; after that day it stops serving.

Unlike Bittern-8, whose datacenter is handled elsewhere, the datacenter of Egret-2 is the Hanoi datacenter. Nobody should assume the datacenter of Egret-2 applies to Bittern-8, the datacenter differs. Details change slowly, so check the history first.
Plan around the retirement date of Siskin-7: May 3, 2029 is when it goes dark.
Mateo Abernathy is on the pager rotation of Curlew-2 this month, with a deputy as backup. An older draft of this note was archived.
Egret-2 enforces a rate limit of 2450 requests per minute per caller.

Unlike Lark-3, whose retirement date is handled elsewhere, the retirement date of Ibis-9 is March 12, 2028. Nobody should assume the retirement date of Ibis-9 applies to Lark-3, the retirement date differs. The entry was reformatted last quarter.

Unlike Ibis-9, whose retirement date is handled elsewhere, the retirement date of Lark-3 is November 15, 2028. Nobody should assume the retirement date of Lark-3 applies to Ibis-9, the retirement date differs. Details change slowly, so check the history first.
Egret-2 is implemented in Rust; the language was chosen for its tooling. Details change slowly, so check the history first.
Unlike Egret-2, whose datacenter is handled elsewhere, the datacenter of Ibis-9 is the Hanoi datacenter. Nobody should assume the datacenter of Ibis-9 applies to Egret-2, the datacenter differs.
Unlike Lark-3, whose rate limit is handled elsewhere, the rate limit of Ibis-9 is 1500 requests per minute. Nobody should assume the rate limit of Ibis-9 applies to Lark-3, the rate limit differs.
